title: Isolate static Docker device mapping across one MK.2 enumeration epoch

claims.statement: Verified H-039 evidence refutes automatic MK.2 reacquisition by the continuously running Companion 4.3.3 container with its static Docker devices mapping: the exact USB serial returned in a new enumeration epoch, configuration and top-level identities remained unchanged, but the unchanged SurfaceThread recovered no hidraw descriptor within 30 seconds.

H-039 observed the same host pathname and rdev before and after reconnect, while the USB device number, HID sysfs path, inode, and ctime changed; therefore pathname and rdev alone do not identify the current enumeration epoch.
claims.evidence: H-039 initial, disconnected, and reconnected host snapshots in the verified run.

claims.statement: The static Docker devices mapping is a plausible stale-device boundary, but H-039 did not isolate it from Companion or its surface module.
claims.evidence: H-039 static compose mapping plus the lost descriptor and absent reopen; causal attribution remains intentionally unresolved.

claims.statement: H-040: across one exact MK.2 disconnect and reconnect, a probe container started before removal retains its static Docker device node identity while a read-only bind of the host device directory observes absence and then the new host node epoch.
claims.evidence: D³ minimal refutation Slice derived from H-039 and a preflight stat comparison; the governed run remains pending.

claims.statement: H-040 does not determine whether Companion can recover with dynamic exposure, whether restarting or recreating Companion is required, or whether any dynamic device mount is acceptable production architecture.

No udev rule, systemd unit, supervisor, rescan, Companion restart, container recreation, native deployment, reboot behavior, rendered pixels, OBS truth, or security acceptance is established by this Slice.

successCriteria.statement: The run binds verified H-039 evidence, the exact Fedora host, graphical principal, exact MK.2 serial, initial host node epoch, probe image identity, source hashes, and active governance contract before asking for physical removal.
successCriteria.verification: Canonical H-039 and governance receipts plus fresh host USB, sysfs, HID, character-node, owner, session, image, and source observations.

successCriteria.statement: One lab-owned probe container created while the MK.2 is present exposes the initial node both through Docker's static device mapping and through a read-only bind of the host device directory, without reading from or writing to the HID device.
successCriteria.verification: Exact docker invocation audit and fs.stat-only receipts for both paths; no Companion, OverlayKit, virtual key invocation, device read, or device write.

successCriteria.statement: During one human-bounded disconnect and reconnect, the host observer proves stable exact absence and a new enumeration epoch, and the probe records both mapping views at initial, absent, and returned stages.
successCriteria.verification: Separate challenge windows, three stable host snapshots per transition, host polling chronology, and container stat receipts.

successCriteria.statement: A supported outcome requires the dynamic directory-bind view to disappear with the host node and return with the exact new host st_dev, inode, ctime, and rdev while the static Docker device view remains the original container node identity; any complete contrary observation refutes H-040.
successCriteria.verification: Schema-valid supported/refuted outcome with independently recomputed epoch and mapping predicates.

successCriteria.statement: Cleanup removes the exact H-040 probe container, leaves the reconnected MK.2 present with no owner reported by the host-scope fuser observation, and records that no production or host configuration was changed.
successCriteria.verification: Exact container absence plus the final host snapshot mount namespace, fuser receipt, and invocation audit; an empty host-scope fuser result does not disprove owners in other namespaces.
